text:
jamie_dev: FYI running canary traffic for runtime 3.2.1 + SDK 4.2 on quant-v3b, seeing a reproducible memory spike after ~1200 tokens. not great for longseq workloads.

deploy-bot: automatic canary check: 3 checks failed (mem, tail-latency). Full logs: https://ci.internal/canary/1723456789 :warning:

alex_w: thanks for flagging. are we talking a regression vs 3.1.x or something new in 3.2.1+4.2 combo?

jamie_dev: baseline 3.1.6 + SDK 4.1 was stable. this shows 30-40% higher RSS growth per request. stack trace points at kvcache allocator loop during long seqs.

ravi_p: can you paste the minimal repro and the head of the logs?

jamie_dev: sure — reproducer curl below. run against canary route.

```\ncurl -sS -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"quant-v3b","runtime":"3.2.1","input":"'"$(python -c "print('x'*1400)")"'","max_tokens":800}'\n```

Logs snippet: ``[kv_alloc] grow from 128mb -> 512mb after token 1203; pid=7845 RSS 3.1g -> 4.3g in 10s``

maria_g: ugh. this is within the scheduled unpin window for runtime 3.2.1 we planned to lift tomorrow. can we delay?

alex_w: propose we hold the unpin for prod. Options: 1) revert runtime to 3.1.6 on canary+staging and continue investigation, 2) apply runtime pin (soft pin) to 3.1.6 for affected model group, 3) try SDK shim to restore kvcache behaviour.

sre_oncall: option 2 sounds safest short term. how disruptive is a soft pin? any client-facing impact?

ravi_p: soft pin is a deploybot operation: `deploy-bot set-pin runtime model-group=quantizing group=quant-v3b version=3.1.6 reason="mem-regression-3.2.1" expires=2024-06-10T18:00Z` — no restart required for serving infra, routing layer will prefer pinned runtime for new allocations. minimal impact.

jamie_dev: can we do a scoped pin only for dedicated + private customers? that avoids changing hosted experiments.

alex_w: yes — deploy-bot supports scope flags. `--scope=dedicated,private`. good call.

maria_g: also want a quick postmortem checklist: add canary test that simulates longseqs for quant models, add regression alert for RSS growth >20% in 5m, and schedule a follow-up to evaluate SDK 4.2 changes to kvcache.

ravi_p: I'm going to run a quick bisect between SDK 4.1/4.2 to see if it's SDK or runtime interplay. will update in ~45m.

deploy-bot: action queued: set-pin runtime=3.1.6 scope=dedicated,private model-group=quant-v3b expires=2024-06-10T18:00Z by=ravi_p. status: pending approval. Use `/deploy approve 1723456789` to approve.

alex_w: approving now. /deploy approve 1723456789 :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: approved and executed. pin created id=pin-8792. routing changed for 12 routes.

jamie_dev: thanks all. I'll keep canary running against an isolated cluster with 3.2.1 while we bisect. tagging @sre_oncall for monitoring during the window.

sre_oncall: monitoring alerts enabled for canary cluster and we set a contact rotation. will escalate if RSS crosses 4.5g.

maria_g: after bisect let's discuss whether to patch runtime, ship an SDK shim, or add a compatibility test that gates unpin windows. prefer automated gate.

ravi_p: quick note: if we do an SDK shim, prefer it as a temporary compatibility layer rather than long-term fix; runtime patch preferred. I'll update with findings.

jamie_dev: closing loop — pin present, canary rollbacks paused. will open a follow-up thread with bisect results and recommended next steps. :memo:
